facts.text: The Australasian grebe is a small waterbird common on fresh water lakes and rivers in greater Australia, New Zealand and nearby Pacific islands.
facts.quote: a small waterbird common on fresh water lakes and rivers in greater Australia, New Zealand and on nearby Pacific islands

facts.text: At 25–27 cm in length, the Australasian grebe is one of the smallest members of the grebe family.
facts.quote: At 25–27 cm (9.8–10.6 in) in length, it is one of the smallest members of the grebe family

facts.text: In breeding plumage, the Australasian grebe has a glossy-black head and neck with a striking chestnut facial stripe from behind the eye to the base of the neck.
facts.quote: Both sexes are dark brown above with a glossy-black head and neck and a striking chestnut facial stripe, extending from behind the eye to the base of the neck

facts.text: The Australasian grebe's eye is yellow, with a prominent pale yellow face spot below.
facts.quote: The eye is yellow, with a prominent pale yellow face spot below.

facts.text: The Australasian grebe usually dives immediately when alarmed and swims away under water.
facts.quote: an excellent swimmer and diver, and usually dives immediately when alarmed and swims away under water

facts.text: The Australasian grebe is not a strong flyer and will fly distances only at night, presumably to avoid predators.
facts.quote: They are not strong flyers and will fly distances only at night, presumably to avoid predators.

facts.text: If disturbed, the Australasian grebe will dive and re-surface 10–15 metres away rather than fly.
facts.quote: If disturbed they will dive and re-surface 10–15 metres away rather than fly.

facts.text: Young Australasian grebes ride on their parents' backs, hidden between their slightly raised wings.
facts.quote: Initially the young will ride on the parents back, hidden between their slightly raised wings.

facts.text: Chicks begin to dive and feed themselves at about 10 weeks, and the mother may then leave, though some return soon after to check on the chicks.
facts.quote: When the chicks begin to dive and feed themselves (at about 10 weeks) the mother may leave too, although mothers have been known to return soon after, apparently to check on the chicks.

facts.text: Parent Australasian grebes drive away ducks and herons by flapping their wings wildly or splashing water at intruders.
facts.quote: will try to drive away other water birds (ducks, herons) by confronting them and flapping their wings wildly or using their wings to splash water at the intruders
